newsitem.title: USA: Schering says forex trimmed Q3 sales 2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Schering says forex trimmed Q3 sales 2 pct.

text.p: Schering-Plough Corp said on Wednesday that foreign exchange, reflecting a stronger U.S. dollar versus most major currencies, trimmed about two percentage points off the company's third quarter sales.
The pharmaceutical company reported third quarter sales of $1.4 billion, up 10 percent over the $1.3 billion recorded in 1995's third quarter.
It reported earnings per share of $0.79, up from $0.68 a year ago and above the First Call consensus estimate of $0.78.

Schering-Plough said its third quarter results were driven by the strong performance of its worldwide ethical pharmaceutical business, which posted a sales gain of 13 percent, or 15 percent when foreign exchange is excluded.
Ethical pharmaceuticals are generally non-generic prescription drugs.

Third quarter worldwide sales of the non-sedating antihistimine Claritin line totaled $323 million, up 73 percent, while sales of the anti-cancer/anti-viral agent Intron A were $138 million, up 21 percent, the company said.
